With the overhaul of changes in the summer, one does wonder what Tare would have done differently, especially with suggestions that his hands were tied in the mercato last season. Nevertheless,

Speaking on Sky Sport’s ‘Calcio Unplugged’, Igli Tare revealed all to Gianluca Di Marzio and Stefano Borghi in an in-depth interview about his time with the Diavolo, as Radio Rossonera has relayed.

“Today is the first time I’ve spoken out after all these months. The wound of not having reached the Champions League is still enormous, and since I arrived at Milan – also questioning myself with the type of contract I signed – the objective couldn’t be only the Champions League; otherwise I wouldn’t have understood where I was.”

“It was great because he was the one who convinced me. He had such a huge desire to join Milan. I wanted to video chat before going to see him because I couldn’t believe it. But after five minutes, I knew in my head that he was the player Milan really lacked.

“Not just because of his qualities, but as a man and as a figure that that team didn’t have. He never said no. A photo with a child, an autograph, a meeting, talking to someone… He never said no. These are the things that humility is key to in life.

“I’m proud to have brought a great champion to Milan. In my opinion, if he wants, he can play another two seasons without any problem. He never missed a training session. Sometimes we were the ones to stop him because he was always there, ready. Loving football at that age is truly an honour.”

Is it a characteristic of the champion or is it a generational issue? Today’s champions seem to have a different mentality:

“Today we live in the age of social media. At 16, you’re already a footballer who can earn millions of euros. Living this way, you have the problem of not only managing a player, who is still a child, but you have to manage the business they bring with them: family, agents, girlfriends…

“These are obstacles that didn’t exist back then. We were a generation that played in the streets. Back then, our parents beat us to get us to come home. Today, however, it’s to get them out of the house because they spend all day in front of computers.

“This aspect has been lost a bit, but it’s our fault. Education and discipline are the key to success.”

Fullkrug. He performed poorly in Milan, but in the Bundesliga he’s scoring a lot and is the top scorer. How do you explain that?

“It’s simple. He came to us after a tough time in England, with a lot of scepticism. And then, right away, he broke his toe. No one ever said he’d been having injections on the bone for two months just to train, let alone to play.

“I knew he was a centre forward that the team was missing; given his characteristics and his interpretation of the game, his qualities were unquestionable. Just two years before coming to Milan, he’d played in the Champions League final, playing a key role in a competition with Borussia Dortmund.

“There are situations where, for a player, even a very important one, it matters how you feel. If you feel appreciated, valued, taken into consideration… When you play for a club like Milan, the weight of the shirt is completely different than when you play for other clubs.

“You feel it from the first day you join. I had no doubt that he could be what he’s demonstrating now.”

“We tried to sign him back in June. We made a first attempt. In the final days of the transfer window, another important name we tried to sign was Akanji. The Champions League was crucial for both of them. They turned him down, not because of the club’s importance, but because he wasn’t playing in the Champions League.

“Then the opportunity arose again at the end of August for Rabiot. Defeat against Cremonese? No, we had already decided to bring him. It was just a matter of contract details.”

“It was difficult for us because we decided to change the formation five days before the transfer window closed. Switching from a 4-3-3 to a three-man defense meant we were having a really hard time finding a quality player in the last five days.

“We were a bit unlucky, first with the Akanji story and then with Liverpool’s Joe Gomez… Guehi’s move from Crystal Palace to Liverpool fell through, and at the last minute they—we already had the deal ready, we were just waiting for this to happen—made a step back. And to avoid being left without a central defender at the last minute, we signed Odogu as a promising player.”

On not being able to reach the Champions League and not being able to continue his work at Milan…

“This is the first time today, after all these months, that I’ve spoken about this… The wound of not reaching the Champions League is still enormous. I think that from the first day I arrived at Milan, even in the way I signed—I questioned myself with the type of contract.

“I said, ‘If I have to come only for the Champions League objective, then I don’t understand where I’ve come from.’ Milan has a different story. I had to go through a trial. The disappointment is that those who run the club didn’t understand how much time people needed, which is now being done, rightly so.

“That is to say, it takes several transfer sessions to get a competitive team ready to win. At the beginning, I felt the responsibility to put the pieces together immediately, because after the defeat in the Coppa Italia final the year before, there were some important signs.

“I didn’t know where to start. But I think we did an important job last summer, we sold for a lot and also signed 10 new players. Then you need time to integrate, learn new philosophies and create a cohesive group, hungry to win.

“Until March-April, we were a group with difficulties, but we were at the top of the table. Then in the last 10 matchdays, we had a mental breakdown, also due to other external dynamics, which I don’t want to discuss here, which had a significant impact.

“Internal or external dynamics? External to the team. But we also have some blame: myself first and foremost, along with Max [Allegri].

“We had to be a little more attentive to certain dynamics. We needed to be more present with the team to ultimately lead them to the final result. Isolation is the wrong word; I don’t believe in these things. I believe in teamwork; I believe in cohesion: from the club to the team.

“When this happens, you transmit it to the team. When these situations become possible, you could also see it in the team’s results, because the players are very attentive. Sometimes we think they have other interests, but they pay attention to everything that comes out. They follow everything very carefully and transmit it.

“Instilling serenity… How can you convey serenity? When, in difficult moments, you show that you believe in the project more than before. Sometimes I missed this feeling, a lack of something that could give us the final push.”

But despite this, did you think you could continue? Does this farewell after only a year feel like a stab in the back?

“Look, I would have asked for a round table where we could all sit down together and analyze everything. Then they could have just said ‘no, thanks’… But I respect the decision they made. I accept it with great regret, but I’ve never questioned it because there’s someone above me who has to decide, including for the fate of the club.

“And when they decide to take a different path, you have to accept it. I know things could have gone differently, even much better. I’ll always be a Milan fan, even after an experience like that.”

Was AC Milan a team that needed the constant presence of a manager or coach to avoid letting itself go as it later did?

“The feeling I had at the beginning was that this leadership was a bit lacking. The arrival of Modric—and another of our goals was also Granit Xhaka, Leverkusen’s captain—was precisely to bring real players into the group, with important characteristics and capable of leading others.

“Granit didn’t arrive; Luka arrived, who has a different way of being a leader: he does it in silence and with his attitude on the pitch. I had the opportunity to meet Mike Maignan: an extraordinary guy, a soul who cares deeply about the AC Milan shirt.

“Gabbia is another extraordinary guy; he lives for this club. Rabiot too… His experience spoke for itself. The great disappointment is that I expected something more in terms of responsibility and leadership from Pulisic: he’s a top-class player with unquestionable qualities. But in terms of performance, things happened that I had never experienced in my career…

“Like Gimenez: an extraordinary guy with numbers that spoke for themselves; for a year he failed to score a goal. Then it happened that Pulisic didn’t score for six months. He scored a goal. Then Leao didn’t score for four months.

“Situations that are hard to come by in football have happened… It can happen that you don’t score for a month, two months, but that long a period of time also affected the team’s final performance.

“Losing a match against Cagliari the way we did, 2-1, I think was the worst match of my life. The feeling and the disappointment I felt towards the fans in the stadium that night is something I will never forget for the rest of my life.”

If Cardinale had been the Cardinale he is today, the one who is also physically present, would you still be AC ​​Milan’s DS?

“I can’t answer that question; he has to answer it. I can say that I remember when the Jashari negotiations were going on… I had just landed in Rome and I was very pleased when he called me because he wanted to understand what was happening in that negotiation.

“I explained all the dynamics to him and I really liked that he said, ‘Anything you need, if you have to spend a little more, let me know because I’m here.’ Then during that process I never had the chance to talk to him, even intentionally.

“There were other people above me who I never wanted to bypass. I never had a direct relationship with him, and the possibility of a discussion would have helped everyone. Not me, but everyone. By putting all the problems and dynamics on the table, we could have resolved things much sooner. But I think it’s a new experience for Cardinale.

“He’s had experience in other sports in America. Now he’s done something important, taking responsibility and putting his face on the line. I would have preferred to have had that presence even when I was there because it would have been very useful. But for the Milan, better late than never.

“Now, for better or worse, he will make his own decisions and responsibilities. I think that for him, too, the best interests of Milan come first.”

Was Leao a problem or a resource in your mind?

“I knew him from the outside. When I had the chance to meet him in person, I thought he was an extraordinary guy. I truly loved him as a person, like everyone else. But he was the player from whom we all expected something more. I think football was no longer a priority for him. That’s the key to understanding him.”

“I think a bit about his life outside of football. Music, fashion, things… But I never doubted the sense of belonging he had towards Milan. You could sense that he loved playing for Milan and was suffering from not performing.

“He had many physical problems… First a calf, then a bit of pubalgia… He always played with his hands under control. I always tried to have individual conversations with him more than with any other Milan player.

“Every time I spoke to him, I left with a positive feeling. I sensed that he wanted to. But sometimes wanting isn’t enough.”

Was there a chance that Leao would leave during your summer too?

“A concrete offer never came for him. Regarding the other transfers, it’s not just Tare’s job. When I arrived – even at Lazio – I was a bit alone, but I tried to involve all the members of the club to give him the importance he needed to build a sense of belonging and responsibility. I think I did a very good job, together with Furlani, Ibra, and Moncada.

“We achieved significant sales figures, in a year when we weren’t even in the Champions League. Thanks to the work we did last summer, investments were made this year, with the money we had at the time. I really believe in teamwork.

“I said it even before the Coppa Italia match against Bari; I asked to speak to convey the importance of the work of the people within the club because it was right that way. Then afterwards, it’s human…

“They were coming off a bad year, when two cumbersome figures like Tare and Allegri arrive, and everyone was talking about Tare and Allegri, some disappointment was understandable. I understood the feeling they had, but I could… There was little to do about it.

“For me, it was a new path, a new opportunity. It was essential to work as a team and present ourselves as a real company.”

#1963. Archie Gray and Hayden Hackney on Scotland's radar as Sebastien Pocognoli looks to tempt stars away from England

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:44 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 17:53 EST, 12 November 2026

Sebastien Pocognoli has revealed that Scotland are stepping up their efforts to persuade players who are eligible for England to wear Dark Blue.

While the Belgian is content with the group of players at his disposal, he admits he and the SFA are in dialogue with certain individuals who, potentially, could improve the squad.

It’s understood that Tottenham’s Archie Gray and Everton’s Hayden Hackney are among the names with whom there are ongoing discussions ahead of the Euro 2028 qualifiers next year.

Both players have represented England – the country in which they were born – at Under-21 level yet could still switch to Scotland through family connections.

‘I have had direct contact or indirect contact,’ the Belgian admitted when asked about similarly eligible players. ‘When I go to the direct contact, it’s because I feel it’s a first positive approach.

‘Yeah, I’ve done it with many players. I’ll do my best to bring them.’

Scotland boss Pocognoli is keen to add to his options and has spoken to potential new recruits

Under Steve Clarke, Scotland tried to persuade Harvey Barnes to switch allegiance only for the Newcastle player to confirm that he felt English.

Prepared to take each case on its merits, Pocognoli explained: ‘With Barnes it was different. The two other lads (Gray and Hackney) are young lads. It’s a long way. But if you wait too long, it might not be the right moment.

‘In a year’s time, we will see. Right now, we have players in the squad who are performing well.

‘It will always be up to them (current players) to be the priority because we’ve built things and we’ve had time with the ones who are here right now.’

While Pocognoli has previously made it clear that he won’t beg any player to pull on a Scotland shirt, he feels it’s incumbent on him and the SFA to gauge the feelings of players down south who could help his side.

‘We are on it,’ he stressed. ‘We are always proactive in all of these situations.

‘What is very exciting about those two names is that they are young players. That’s interesting.

Archie Gray's dad Andy, uncle Eddie and grandfather Frank all represented Scotland

‘We have to look and manage the situation. But it won’t be a definitive choice from them because we weren’t proactive. That has to be clear. We are proactive.

‘The best way to convince players is to show good football, show them they can come to us, enjoy it and be successful. They have to feel when they leave a top club that they arrive here into top conditions and a top environment.

‘That’s the best publicity we can offer, to show good football. In the end, it’s a human decision, a feeling.

‘I didn’t have that case. With my Italian blood, maybe I wasn’t that good! But I can understand the feeling of what it’s like to have to choose a country, with your background, family, football education and social circle.

‘So, it’s not easy. But it’s always a feeling from inside and I need to feel it. When I feel it, I’ll try to be on it.’

Hayden Hackney has impressed for Everton this season and has played for Scotland Under-21s

Meanwhile, Pocognoli believes a fully fit Kieran Tierney can have a major role to play in his new-look side.

While the preferred systems of his predecessors meant accommodating the Celtic man and Andy Robertson could be a conundrum, the 3-4-3 which the Belgian deploys seems better suited to fielding the pair at the same time.

With Tierney back in contention to face North Macedonia after pulling out of the last squad through injury, the manager said: ‘He will bring a different profile. He has a fantastic left foot and is an experienced player who knows the squad and knows what it means to play for Scotland. It is a big plus. He trained very well this week and is very focused.

‘He can play different positions. He can play left-back, he can play in the back three, as he has in the past. He plays left-back for Celtic, but in some games he has inverted. He can also bring some offensive attributes in the back three. We are lucky to have someone with that profile.

‘It is always a challenge to try to make all the players shine in the best shape possible. We have strong competition on the left side.

‘We have quality players. I will try to find the best balance and make everybody shine. If we can play Kieran and Andy in the same team if they are fit, it is a plus for the team.’

Kieran Tierney has been tipped to have a big impact for Scotland under Pocognoli

Pocognoli is desperate to secure his first victory at Hampden this evening having tasted defeat in his first two home games with Switzerland and Slovenia.

‘I haven’t really experienced Hampden yet and I’d like to,’ he said. ‘I was frustrated in the first game (against the Swiss) because I thought we started quite good in the first 10 minutes.

‘Then we know what happened (red card for Jack Hendry). In the last game, it was just disappointment.

‘It’s important that we play a consistent game and combine a good result with good football. If we play average and win, I’ll be happy with three points.

‘But the process is to play good football as well. It’s important that we excite the fans and we have the players for that. I hope that we deliver what we’ve worked on in the last four days.’

#1962. ‘Good fit’ – Michael Owen backs Mauricio Pochettino to ‘reignite’ Man Utd star

Michael Owen believes that Mauricio Pochettino has the managerial nous to get Marcus Rashford back to his best in a Manchester United shirt.

Rashford failed to make an impact under Michael Carrick after returning to Old Trafford following his loan spell at Barcelona last season.

The 29-year-old is yet to score in the Premier League this season and missed the last five matches of Carrick’s tenure due to a hip injury.

Rashford now has a fresh opportunity to revive his United career under Pochettino after the Argentine signed a two-and-a-half-year deal to replace Carrick.

And having previously tried to sign Rashford at Paris Saint-Germain, Owen believes that Pochettino could be the perfect manager to get the best out of the English forward.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘Quite a few have tried,’ Owen told Metro. ‘It’s very hard to say. It’s the million-dollar question.

‘Everybody has their different views, but Poch has a reputation of bringing players through young players and reigniting players. He’s a top manager.

‘He’s been there, seen it, and done it at various different levels. So, he’d have as good a chance as anybody to reignite certain players.

‘It’s not like Rashford has been awful since he’s been at Manchester United, he’s done pretty well, but I’m sure there’s more in there and I’m sure Pochettino could be a good fit for him.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Elsewhere, Owen urged Pochettino to resist calls to cash in on United captain Bruno Fernandes after he turned down the club’s latest offer of a new deal.

‘Manchester United aren’t in the luxurious position of having 20 world-class players,’ he added. ‘They’ve probably got a small handful and he is one of them.

‘How weak do you want to make the team? You need to build on the good players you’ve got.

‘I know he’s opened his mouth a little bit in recent times. He’s probably not the flavour of the month, but he’s probably been the only shining light in that Manchester United team for the last eight years or something. So, no, I would definitely not be selling him.’

#1961. Manchester United injury update: Latest news and return dates as Mauricio Pochettino takes charge

Mauricio Pochettino could be boosted by some returnees as he faces the first match of his Manchester United tenure on Sunday.

Today, Wednesday, November 18, is officially the first day of the Argentine’s tenure with United, and once he arrives at Carrington he will throw himself headlong into preparing for his first match.

That will come just five days after his arrival in the form of a trip to Anfield, to face Liverpool.

High on his to-do list will be figuring out who is or is not fit to make that journey across the north-west, and there is no shortage of patients in the physio’s room.

Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw and Carlos Baleba are the most notable absentees, but Pochettino stands to welcome a number of fit-again stars back into the squad this week.

With that in mind, here is all the latest Manchester United injury news and potential return dates...

Marcus Rashford has not featured for United since the defeat by Atletico Madrid in October, when he picked up a persistent hip issue.

He had been pushing to return against Aston Villa but did not feature in the matchday squad, and has spent the international break building up his fitness at Carrington.

Michael Carrick had described Rashford’s injury as “day-by-day” before he left the United job, and it is hoped he will be able to return at Anfield.

Potential return date: Sunday, November 22 vs Liverpool (A)

Luke Shaw has been sidelined with a muscle injury since early October, but is thought to be pushing for a return to fitness.

As of the Aston Villa draw, Shaw had yet to return to training, but reports during the international break suggest he is pushing for a comeback at Anfield.

JJ Gabriel confirms Man Utd exit with emotional farewell statement

Man Utd target issues transfer update amid contract limbo: ‘We’ll see’

His return would be a huge boost for Pochettino and United, given the squad lacks a clear backup for Shaw at left-back.

Potential return date: Sunday, November 22 vs Liverpool (A)

The summer signing Carlos Baleba has made a stuttering start to this campaign as he struggles for fitness.

He arrived from Brighton with an ankle injury, which he shook off to make a run of appearances, before tweaking his hamstring against Roma earlier this month.

Speaking at the time, Carrick explained Baleba is facing weeks out and would not return during the international break.

Patrick Dorgu missed a stretch of this campaign after suffering a hamstring injury in the September international break, but returned to put in an impressive cameo against Aston Villa last time out.

It seems, though, that he is not yet fully fit. He joined up with the Danish national team for the November international break and traied with his team-mates, but was promptly sent home due to fitness concerns.

“He's still on his way back. The fact that he got those minutes against Aston Villa and did a fantastic job should be taken with a grain of salt,” said head coach Brian Riemer. “There are still some lingering issues with the major muscle injury he suffered. We need to make sure it doesn't flare up again. We're optimistic, and we also believe things will go well.”

A statement issued by the Danish FA when he left camp said he was not match fit, but it is hoped he will be able to feature in the Anfield match.

Potential return date: Sunday, November 22 vs Liverpool (A)

Harry Maguire was forced off at half-time of the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa with a back injury.

He had come into the match with a knock but pushed through it to start, but did not last long thereafter.

Carrick explained it was a back spasm which forced hi off, adding: "I don't know how bad it is but, going into the internationals, there should be plenty of time for him to recover."

Potential return date: Sunday, November 22 vs Liverpool (A)

Benjamin Sesko has been ruled out until the new year with a niggling shin injury.

The big Slovenian missed the latter stages of last season and the early days of the current campaign after suffering an injury at Old Trafford in May.

He enjoyed a run in the side and appeared to be back at full fitness, but has since been sidelined again having reaggravated the initial issue.

It is hoped a lengthy rest will allow him to fully recover without undergoing surgery.

Speaking before being sacked, Carrick said: “We're not exactly sure yet how long [he will be out for], but it's going to be a significant amount of time, unfortunately.

“So I feel for Ben, he had the issue at the end of last season that we looked after and tried to give him as much time to recover and then unfortunately he's had the issue coming into this season.

“So, we've got to do what's best for Ben and he's going to have to have some time on the sidelines, unfortunately.

Manuel Ugarte is currently recovering after undergoing surgery on a ruptured ACL suffered at the World Cup. He is expected to miss most, if not all, of the 2026/27 season.

#1960. England star told to snub Chelsea and join ‘bigger’ club Arsenal

Bournemouth sensation Alex Scott should set his sights ‘higher’ than Chelsea and aim to join ‘one of the biggest teams in Europe’ like Arsenal.

That’s according to Chris Waddle, who claims Scott has taken his game ‘to a new level’ over the last 18 months and is looking more and more like the ‘complete’ central midfielder.

Waddle’s comments come amid mounting speculation over Scott’s future, with Bournemouth bracing themselves for incoming offers to steal their prized possession away in the January transfer window.

Scott’s eye-catching breakthrough in the international arena has done little to quieten rumours that the 23-year-old could soon be destined for bigger and better things, with Chelsea, Arsenal, Manchester City and Tottenham all rumoured to be circling.

Though Scott is currently sidelined with a thigh injury, his stock continues to soar – and it’s understood the Cherries could be prepared to do business should they receive a bid in excess of £80m this winter.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

In an interview with iGaming.com, ex-England international Waddle revealed how he had been keeping close tabs on Scott’s progress since he was first alerted to his potential at Bristol City.

‘I’ve always liked Alex Scott. I think he’s a lovely, cultured player. There’s no doubt in my mind that in the last eighteen months, the kid’s taken his game to a new level,’ Waddle explained.

‘I followed him at Bristol City, and when he was there, I was speaking to someone that knew him who told me he was a Tottenham fan.

‘Tottenham have been collecting players in the last six months, but he is a top-class player and someone that would walk into any squad.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Will they move for him? It seems unlikely given the midfielders they signed in the summer.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Chelsea are reportedly leading the hotly contested race to sign Scott and are said to be increasingly confident of reaching an agreement with Bournemouth for the central midfielder.

However, Waddle insists Scott should ideally be aiming higher than a move to Stamford Bridge, name-checking Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal as potential options.

‘According to reports, Chelsea retain the strongest interest in him. No disrespect to them, but I think he can look higher. I think he’s got the ability to play for the biggest teams in Europe: Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, PSG, Arsenal,’ he added.

‘The guy looks like he’s a top player to me. He looks like he’s only going to get better. If I was a manager or a sporting director and I needed a midfielder, I would be looking at him.

‘He’s a complete midfielder. He can play as a 10, an 8, and a 6. He offers you a bit of everything. He reminds me a little bit of Rodri in the way that he likes to take the ball off the centre-back and start making things happen.

‘His composure and technique make him a standout player for any team looking to sign someone who can run a midfield and control the tempo.’

While Bournemouth are in no hurry to part with Scott, the club’s hierarchy recognise that the England international may have ambitions to move on elsewhere near future.

For now, though, the Cherries are adamant that the Vitality Stadium remains the ‘right place’ for Scott.

‘At this point, we’re convinced that we’re the right place for Alex to be, for Alex to stay, and we’ll keep on addressing contract issues with Alex as we move through this year,’ Bournemouth owner Bill Foley told talkSPORT last month.

‘We’d love to have Alex stay here, sign a new contract and be part of this team for the long haul, and we’re still working on it. We haven’t given up.

‘But sometimes players get stars in their eyes and they think that Chelsea is the right place to go or Manchester City.’

Scott’s current contract on the south coast runs through to June 2028.

After starting last season in eye-catching fashion, Town fell away by mid-autumn. This time around, they are showing more stamina and aptitude.

#1958. When will Mauricio Pochettino arrive at Manchester United? Travel plans revealed after final USMNT fixture

The dawn of the Mauricio Pochettino era is upon us, with the Argentine having taken to the dugout with the United States for the final time on Tuesday evening.

Pochettino is returning to the Premier League for a fourth time, replacing Michael Carrick as head coach of Manchester United.

He is facing a sizeable rescue mission, with Man United languishing in 18th in the Premier League having won just one of their first ten matches. He faces a tricky start, too, with Liverpool, Sporting CP, and Brentford on the docket for his first matches in charge.

While Carrick was formally dismissed last week, after the Man Utd hierarchy held crisis talks regarding his future in Monaco, Pochettino has been delayed in actually starting his new role.

He first had to see out one last international break with the United States national team, which involved a two-legged tie against Haiti, before returning to England.

Pochettino’s term as Manchester United manager will officially begin today, November 18, 2026, as confirmed in a club statement last week.

That start date was chosen to allow him to lead the United States national team through their two Concacaf Nations League matches this international break, a two-legged tie against Haiti. The second of those two legs kicked off at midnight on Tuesday night for UK viewers.

The Argentine was set to travel to Manchester immediately after the match, on a private jet laid on by United. That will see him touch down in the north-west on Wednesday morning.

Pochettino is expected to head straight from the airport to Carrington, where he will throw himself headlong into preparing for Sunday’s trip to Anfield.

Some of his backroom staff arrived on location in Manchester ahead of Pochettino, however, laying some groundwork before the head coach’s own arrival.

#1957. Doncaster Rovers boss Grant McCann on when football talk is off the menu with son Bayley

Rovers' worrying recent form may have provided food for thought for both, given their working relationship at the club as manager and player.

But from a family perspective, time together as father and son – away from a work environment - is also beneficial and important for both.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Rovers boss, whose side makes the trip to Yorkshire rivals Bradford City on Saturday, said: "We don't really (talk about football). We just either go for something to eat or go out to the cinema or something like that and we just think about everything but (football) really.

"Just life and how he's getting on and all that sort of stuff.

"On most Thursday evenings, I'll take him out for a bit of food and just spend that little bit of time with him because I don't get to see him even though he's here every day.

"I don't get to spend that sort of time with him like I do with my two youngest boys.

"So we always go out and (usually) have something to eat. He's still hasn't paid yet!"

McCann's son (pictured) has made the breakthrough at first-team level this term at Rovers, having joined on a two-and-a-half year deal from South Yorkshire rivals Barnsley in the winter window.

The young midfielder, who turns 21 early next month, made his Rovers debut from the bench in the home game against Stevenage in late April.

He followed up with another substitute appearance at Peterborough United, a club both father and son know well, on the final day of the 2025-26 campaign.

McCann has kicked on this term, with his development recognised by an international call-up to Northern Ireland Under-21 side. He netted in the fixture against Malta in late September.

On the club front, McCann has made 13 appearances in all competitions for Rovers and scored his maiden goal for the club in the League One game at Luton Town on October 27.

According to reports, Glasgow Rangers recently sent scouts to monitor the form of McCann.

For McCann senior, it's very much business during working hours with his son, which is just the way that both want it.

He continued: "I want to be his manager when I'm in here and when we're away from here, I want to be his dad.

"That's just the relationship that we have and I think he prefers it like that.

"It's not like he gets any sort of special treatment or anything or I let him away (with anything).

"If anything, I'll probably speak to him less because I don't want to put any sort of pressure on him.

"I want him to just do his own thing. We still have phone calls now and again.

"He phoned me (recently) telling me his wi-fi was playing up at home, so me and my wife were trying to sort that out for him and it's things like that."

#1955. “Important to take time” – Gabbia admits January return is possible with right precautions

Matteo Gabbia has admitted that he could return to the field in January for AC Milan, but he doesn’t want to rush back.

It has been a difficult season for Milan, at least where injuries are concerned. In defence, they have had issues reminiscent of the 2023/24 season, where Gabbia had to be brought back from his loan spell at Villarreal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This season, though, it seems Gerry Cardinale is going to go down a different route and spend to help Ruben Amorim with his defensive options. Indeed, there have been plenty of rumours about recruitments at the back.

However, Gabbia could again be a key returnee in January, with him hoping to return from injury early in the new year.

Speaking to Sky Sport (via MilanNews) – at an event organised by the Milan Foundation at Milan’s “Arturo Toscanini” secondary school, where they met with several children with disabilities – Gabbia discussed the importance of the event, as well as his recovery.

“It’s wonderful, very enjoyable to spend hours with them. It’s also beautiful to see how they manage to create a group, something that really shows the importance of teamwork, the importance of friendship, even among themselves.

“We’re happy; we thank Fondazione Milan for the project, which is always beautiful and important: we’re happy to be a part of it and we’re enjoying the afternoon.”

Are you able to rejoin the group in January?

“Yes, that could be the time: we’re trying to work hard and do everything as best we can. I obviously have to thank the physiotherapists and the doctor because we’re really doing everything we can every day to try to heal the injury and get back on the pitch feeling good.

“It’s definitely been an unlucky season for me so far: I don’t want it to happen again or for any recurrences, so it’s also important to take the right time, get back in shape, and support the team right now.”

“Although it’s bad for the team that there are so many injured players, we’re together right now, supporting each other and trying to encourage each other through therapy, gym work, and the entire recovery process. Therefore, we’re trying to work as a team this week too, to overcome all the players’ injuries.

“From a personal standpoint, I’m trying to take this time calmly, in the sense that these things are part of sport, part of life, and not all moments are the same.

“This is certainly a difficult time, but it still allows me to stay close to the team, to try to lend my support, even in the good and bad times. That’s what I’m doing, in addition to obviously doing what I can to try to return as soon as possible and make my contribution on the pitch.”

How do you explain the team’s ups and downs?

“I think it’s something we need to get our heads around; we need to understand the importance of every game.

“The other day I heard our coach give an interview in which he said something important: we need to understand that every game, when you don’t win, is taken as a defeat, a heavy defeat. We need to truly understand the importance of every game and approach training to prepare 100%, as best as possible, for every match.

“Therefore, I think this is room for improvement, but I see a group that is really eager to improve, to work, and as a result, I’m sure we’ll be able to fix this flaw as well.

“Although we’ve had a good start to the year in the league and less so in the Europa League, we have plenty of time to improve and have a strong year.”

#1953. Who will England face in Nations League quarter-final? Next opponents confirmed after Spain win

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals as group winners ahead of world champions Spain.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England then beat Spain in a one-game shootout in Madrid to win the group and with that, potentially securing, an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

As a result of finishing top in Group A3, England’s confirmed potential Nations League quarter-final opponent are Belgium and the Netherlands after they were pipped to top spot in Group A1 and A2 by France and Germany respectively.

England’s remaining possible quarter-final opponents was revealed on Tuesday night as Norway produced a stunning comeback from 2-0 down pip Denmark to the runners-up spot behind Portugal in Group A4 by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1951. Trey Nyoni names Arsenal star as ‘toughest opponent’

Liverpool youngster Trey Nyoni has picked out Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard as the ‘toughest opponent’ he has faced at the start of his career.

Odegaard has returned to his sparkling best this season, starting all ten of Arsenal’s opening matches in the Premier League with the reigning champions sitting five points clear at the summit.

Having managed just one goal across the Gunners’ title-winning campaign last term, the 27-year-old appears to have rediscovered his scoring boots, finding the net on five occasions in all competitions this term.

It was Odegaard’s 72nd-minute strike that proved the difference before the international break, when Mikel Arteta’s men were made to work for their victory at home to newly promoted Hull City.

The Norway international will no doubt be desperate to pick up where he left off when the north London giants return to top-flight against at Newcastle on Saturday evening.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Nyoni has himself enjoyed an impressive start to the season at Liverpool and locked horns with Odegaard when the pair did battle at Anfield at the start of the month.

And while Nyoni was taken off before the hour-mark on Merseyside, it’s clear Odegaard left a big impression on the 19-year-old in the 58 minutes his opposite number was on the pitch.

Asked to name the ‘toughest’ player he has come up against, Nyoni told The Inside Scoop, ‘For me personally, I would say Odegaard,’ as he looked back on that afternoon.

‘The way he plays, it’s very busy, moving around and always looking for an option.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘It’s not easy as a midfielder. I think when you play against someone who is constantly moving, you know in the back of your mind that he could be here, but the next minute he’s there.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

When asked if Odegaard perhaps doesn’t get the credit he deserves, Nyoni replied: ‘Yeah, I think the game is evolving and I think nowadays people look at No.10s and automatically think that if they’re not getting goals and assists, they’re not good.

‘For example, in our team we’ve got Flo [Wirtz]. I think Flo does a lot of stuff that people don’t really see.

‘I think what he brings to the team benefits the team. Just because he’s not scoring or assisting, doesn’t mean he’s not effective.

‘Nowadays, the idea that if a player isn’t getting goals or assists, they’re useless, but every player has their own role in the team.

‘Odegaard and people like Flo, if they’re not getting goals and assists, people that don’t watch the game automatically think they haven’t played well but that’s not how football works.’

In the aftermath of Arsenal’s nervy win over Hull, club legend Paul Merson said Odegaard had been ‘like a new signing’ for Arteta this season.

‘He’s been outstanding. He’s the only one really that moves it quickly,’ Merson said of Odegaard on Sky Sports.

‘He moves it quickly, he moves, he gets into positions. I just thought too many players took too many touches and they slowed it down and gave Hull half a chance.

‘I think he’s been outstanding this season, he’s like a new signing for them and he’s been the man so far.

‘Not great but just a good result for Arsenal. But again, he was one of the stars of the show.’

#1950. When is Nations League draw? Start time, confirmed pot numbers and TV channel for quarter-finals

The 2026-27 Nations League draw for the quarter-finals takes place this week, as the business end of the competition comes into focus.

England are among the eight teams to have qualified for the knockout phase, with Thomas Tuchel’s side enjoying a near perfect group phase.

Their only defeat came against reigning world champions Spain on matchday one in September, though the Three Lions exacted revenge on Sunday night as they held on after being reduced to 10-men to seal a famous victory.

As a result, England topped Group A3 at Spain’s expense due to a superior goal difference and that means they are likely to avoid another European heavyweight in the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere, France sealed top spot in Group A1 with a 2-1 win over Turkey, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to finish as runners-up.

In A2, Germany topped the table with a 5-0 thrashing of the Netherlands, who slipped to second on goal difference after such a swing.

Portugal’s position was Group A4 was confirmed after their win over Wales on Tuesday night, though it is Norway joining them in the knockout phases following a remarkable comeback win against Denmark.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place on Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

As well as the quarter-final draw, the promotion/relegation play-offs draw will also be conducted.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The Nations League draw will take place in Nyon, Switzerland.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

The four group winners will be seeded in Pot 1, with the four runners-up will be unseeded in Pot 2.

Pot 1: France, England, Germany, Portugal

Pot 2: Belgium, Spain, Netherlands, Norway

*Portugal are guaranteed a Nations League quarter-final spot, though can still finish first or second in Group A4.

The Nations League quarter-finals, as well as the League A/B and League B/C promotion/relegation play-offs, will be played in March 2027.

The first-legs are scheduled for March 25-27, with the return legs scheduled for March 28-30.

The final tournament is scheduled for June 2027.

Melvin Bard’s former teammate Morgan Schneiderlin is “certain” there is more to come from the Leeds United defender.

Leeds signed Bard on loan from Nice on the final day of the summer transfer window and there is an option to make his move permanent.

The 26-year-old has found himself behind Gabriel Gudmundsson in the left wing-back department but made an impressive appearance from the bench in Leeds’ 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur before the international break.

Former Manchester United and Southampton midfielder Schneiderlin, who played with Bard at Nice, has compared him to Red Devils star Luke Shaw.

He told ComeOn: “I played with Melvin Bard at Nice and saw his development first-hand. When he first arrived, he was already a good player. I compare his progression a bit to Luke Shaw.

“He put in a lot of work on his conditioning and physique during his early time at Nice. He did the work, and now he is much fitter.

“He's very difficult to beat one-v-one, possesses great stamina, and has a very good left foot. Ultimately, whether to stay will be his choice, but he's a quality player and I'm certain he still has plenty of room to improve even further.”

Gudmundsson has established himself among Daniel Farke’s most trusted lieutenants since his arrival in the summer of 2025 and could prove difficult to dislodge.

Bard, however, will have his sights set on a more prominent role heading towards the end of the calendar year.

After putting pen to paper at Elland Road in the summer, Bard said: “Playing in the Premier League has always been a dream of mine, ever since I was a child.

“Leeds is a historic club in the Premier League so it was an easy choice. Leeds has a great history which makes the club an attractive one.

#1948. ‘Back in Leeds’ - Leeds United’s forgotten man Mateo Joseph ‘focused on comeback’ as he shares update

Leeds United forward Mateo Joseph has declared he is “focused on the comeback” as he plots a return to the pitch.

The 23-year-old succumbed to an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in March, while out on loan at Mallorca in La Liga.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He had requested a move away from Elland Road in the previous summer and scored two goals across 30 outings in Spain before being sidelined.

Joseph is now back on British shores, rehabilitating with the help of specialists at Leeds.

Posting on Instagram, the former Spain and England youth international said: “Back in Leeds, focused on the comeback.

“Every day brings progress, every step takes me closer, things are looking up and we’re moving in the right direction. One step at a time.”

It is hard to envisage Joseph carving out a future at Leeds given the progress made by the club since his loan departure.

Whites boss Daniel Farke does not boast a wealth of forward options, yet Joseph would arguably find it tough to leapfrog Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha in the pecking order.

Speaking to The Yorkshire Post in the summer, Leeds icon Jermaine Beckford said: “Mateo has got talent. He's got technical ability. He's got good pace about him as well. We've seen when he's been with the under-21s how good he is at finishing.

“He's had a couple of decent goals as well for the first team, I remember the Chelsea game at Stamford Bridge. He's got it, he just needs to knuckle down, get rid of the external noise, focus on working his socks off, and I think he could [force his way back in].

“Do I think Daniel Farke and the hierarchy want to keep him knowing that he could possibly upset the apple cart? I'm not entirely sure. But it's for Mateo to come back and show that this is a new and improved version of himself. He's got the ability.”

#1947. New Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino reacts to ‘city is blue’ comment with six-word promise

Mauricio Pochettino has said to “give him time” to make Manchester United the dominant club in the city again as he prepares to start work.

Pochettino will take charge of Man United for the first time against Liverpool on Sunday after being appointed to succeed Michael Carrick, who was sacked last week with the club sitting 18th in the Premier League table.

The Argentine’s return to club management has been delayed after being allowed to finish up his commitments with the United States national team.

His last game ended in a 2-0 win for USA against Haiti in Cincinnati during the early hours on Wednesday (UK time) to wrap up an 8-0 aggregate victory in their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final.

AC Milan forward Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with a spectacular overhead kick and teenager Julian Hall doubled the hosts’ lead before half-time.

After bidding an emotional farewell to the USA supporters inside the stadium, Pochettino immediately turned his attentions to the task at hand with Man United and the rivalry with Manchester City.

Told by former Man City loanee DaMarcus Beasley that “Manchester is blue, it will always be blue” in the TNT Sports US studio after the game, Pochettino responded: “You will see. Give me time.

“The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it’s adrenalin you want to feel.

“We need to add our common sense… we know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United, the fan base is amazing.”

Pochettino heads to Old Trafford tasked with steering Man United out of the relegation zone before he can target winning titles and eventually usurping Man City as the dominant team in the city.

United have not been crowned Premier League champions since Sir Alex Ferguson retired, with the legendary Scotsman final season being the last time the club finished above their neighbours in the table.

Additional reporting by Press Association.

#1946. Man Utd plot move for La Liga star Mauricio Pochettino says can be ‘the best in the world’

Manchester United could push for Villarreal full-back Alex Freeman in January, a player Mauricio Pochettino has tipped to become ‘one of the best in the world’ in his position.

Pochettino was confirmed as Michael Carrick’s successor last week and will arrive in Manchester today ahead of his first game in charge away to Liverpool this weekend.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager will be backed in the January transfer window with a striker and a full-back thought to be priorities.

USA international Folarin Balogun is reportedly a target United are considering to bolster their options up top. The Daily Telegraph report another name has been discussed in Freeman, a player Pochettino is a huge admirer of.

The right-back joined Villarreal in January 2026, thriving under head coach Inigo Perez and emerging as an important member of the first-team. Having started out as a winger, he has established himself at right-back, having also played on the left.

#1945. Derby agendas for Barnsley FC, Bradford City, Doncaster Rovers, Huddersfield Town and Sheffield Wednesday

Barnsley and Doncaster Rovers - down among the dead men in League One - will be hoping that rings true as they seek precious shafts of light following arduous autumns.

They face back-to-back derbies in their next two fixtures, which will assume importance not just for the morale of each club, but also for Daniel Stendel and Grant McCann in their second spells at the Reds and Rovers.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sheffield Wednesday, Bradford City and Huddersfield Town have their own motivations to contend with.

In the second half of last autumn, Barnsley slipped up at home to Rotherham United, who won in the league at Oakwell for the first time in 15 visits since March 1969. But they did afford themselves the fillip of three points at Doncaster 14 days later.

The Reds, who welcome the Owls on Friday before visiting Bradford - managed by ex-boss Michael Duff - next Tuesday, would probably settle for a 50 per cent derby ratio this time around.

More especially given that their grim winless league run - nine matches and counting - has descended into a crisis.

They must make do without top-scorer and suspended captain Cameron McGeehan on Friday, while defender Jack Shepherd, a boyhood Wednesdayite, is also banned. The return of Patrick Kelly from international duty with Northern Ireland is a much more welcome development.

The sight of in-form Owls striker and Reds old boy Davis Keillor-Dunn compounding their autumnal angst certainly wouldn't be.

A match-winning display from DKD - who has struck in his last three Wednesday matches - would put the tinlid on things for Reds followers, whose expectation levels are exceedingly low heading into Friday.

If things turn sour, the mood in the home stands has the potential to turn mutinous towards the club hierarchy. Barnsley are without a league win since September 2 and are only kept off the bottom of the table by goal difference. A protest from fans group Tykes Union is planned beforehand.

Derbies brought out the best in McCann's Rovers in League One last season and their recent 2-0 win over Wednesday keeping to that theme.

Rovers secured a derby double against arch-rivals Rotherham for the first time since 1949-50 and made history by winning league games at Barnsley and Millers in the same season.

McCann's side also beat Town and Bradford at home and performed very well in both away games and were extremely unlucky to lose both.

They visit the Bantams on Saturday, seeking to get back onside with supporters following dreadful away performances in their last two matches in league and cup - an embarrassing 3-0 FA Cup loss at non-league Kidderminster and an equally atrocious 6-1 league beating at MK Dons.

On both occasions, McCann issued an apology to travelling fans with some starting to openly question his future. The Rovers chief, whose side host high-flying Town next Thursday, prides himself as being a fighter.

Wednesday’s derby form this term has been in keeping with their wretched numbers on that count over the past couple of years.

They have won just once in their past 14 league fixtures against White Rose counterparts.

So far this season, they were bullied in the second half of their meeting with Bradford in their opening home league fixture of 2026-27 - a 1-0 defeat which was more emphatic than the scoreline sounded.

By common consent, they were somewhat fortunate to secure a late point at Huddersfield on October 10 - when Town were very much the architects of their own downfall.

A fortnight later, a disjointed, unsatisfactory performance at Doncaster proved the final straw for the Owls hierarchy regarding Henrik Pedersen.

Historically, Oakwell at least provides rather happier memories for the Owls, notwithstanding their last visit. They have lost just once on their last eight trips up the A61.

After dismal displays - not just results - in three derby losses at Valley Parade, the Club Doncaster Sports Village and Oakwell last season, redressing the balance would be a barometer of Town’s progress in 26-27.

It’s a case of so far, so good with the Terriers avenging last season’s anaemic loss at Bradford with a cathartic victory on Hallowe’en. Statistically speaking, the visitors’ 3-0 triumph was their biggest ever at BD8.

They have two other scores to settle. Town were fitful in their 3-1 defeat at Oakwell last August and it was a sign of things to come for ex-head coach Lee Grant. They visit Barnsley on December 19.

There were jeers and opprobrium following a tepid 1-0 reverse in Doncaster on a February night when Town’s top-six pitch was exposed.

The present-day worries belong to Rovers. And Barnsley.

#1944. “It is an honour” – Yormark speaks after Milan Sport & Entertainment CEO appointment

Earlier today, AC Milan were introduced to a new name, thanks to the creation of a new company: Milan Sports & Entertainment.

The international break is never really a period of major news, yet Milan broke that spell today. Indeed, RedBird Capital Partners published a statement about a new company formed to oversee all of the Rossoneri’s business.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A centralised company that would allow everything Diavolo to be kept in one place is a major step forward for the club and city. San Donato was mentioned as an important focus for the new company, but the headline will remain the footballing operation.

To help with the project, Gerry Cardinale – who spoke about the decision – has appointed Brett Yormark to be the CEO of the company and reports suggest that he will join in January.

Speaking today, via MilanNews, Yormark admitted it was an honour to be part of the Milan family.

“It is an honour and a privilege to take on this role in a city with Milan’s history and passion for sports. I understand the responsibility that comes with leading an organisation tied to institutions that mean so much to their fans and the communities they serve.

“Throughout my career, I have helped evolve sports organisations, expand their reach, and create new opportunities. I look forward to leveraging this experience to realise RedBird’s vision for MSE.

“I am thrilled to work alongside Gerry, RedBird, and our colleagues in Milan to transform this vision into concrete, lasting results.”

#1943. How Manchester United could line up in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game vs Liverpool as big calls made

The Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United is officially underway, and his first game is just days away.

The Red Devils return from the final international break of 2026 to face the daunting prospect of visiting arch-rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend.

Pochettino inherits a side with just one win in 10 top-flight games this term, a string of results that have left Man Utd in the relegation zone.

The Argentine’s style of play centres around a high-press and an ability to build from the back - two things United have struggled with so far this season.

Injuries across the pitch will impact Pochettino’s selection, with Carlos Baleba and Benjamin Sesko definitely ruled out for the trip to Anfield.

In goal, Senne Lammens is established first-choice and that is unlikely to change with Pochettino’s arrival, while the Argentine might be tempted to copy Michael Carrick and play Leny Yoro at right-back, instructing the Frenchman to tuck in and form a three-man defence in possession.

However, Diogo Dalot will likely start at right-back, with a much more simple defensive approach.

Yoro could therefore partner Ayden Heaven in the heart of defence to give United a bit more pace than a backline featuring Harry Maguire, but the experience of Lisandro Martinez may be hard to ignore as Pochettino balances a squad lacking in confidence.

Patrick Dorgu is a doubt after being sent home from international duty with Denmark, but is said to be winning his battle to be fit for the Anfield trip and could replicate what Antonee Robinson did for Pochettino at left-back.

With the USA, Pochettino had settled on a 4-3-3 formation, with the midfield featuring a sitting player behind two more proactive team-mates.

Pochettino’s immediate issue with the Man United squad will be the fact that there is no clear candidate as a holding midfielder. The injured Baleba does well at screening the backline, but his strengths rely on driving forward with the ball.

It is a similar story for Andrey Santos - a midfielder that is still unsure whether his best position is as a No6, 8, or 10.

The deep-lying playmaker role is a battle between Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans. Pochettino has shown a tendency to trust young, talented players, so it would not be a surprise to see the former Tottenham manager try and work his magic with Mainoo.

Tielemans could play the box-to-box role alongside Mainoo, offering experience during the transition to Pochettino’s ideal approach.

While Pochettino has utilised a deeper player in the middle of the park with the USA, it is likely that he will instead have to build a more attacking midfield at United.

That is because club captain Bruno Fernandes is clearly the Red Devils’ best player, which merits his inclusion.

Matheus Cunha looks a good fit on the left wing as a creative spark, while Bryan Mbeumo’s pace down the right wing would allow Pochettino to create a similar attacking shape to his USA side.

However, with United’s striking options limited, it would not be a surprise to see Mbeumo lead the line, with Amad Diallo playing instead on the right.

Predicted Manchester United XI vs Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Martinez, Dorgu; Tielemans, Mainoo; Amad, Fernandes, Cunha; Mbeumo

#1942. ‘I think he’s the future’ - Leeds United and England star James Trafford gets Steven Gerrard seal of approval

Leeds United star James Trafford has been described as “the future” of England’s goalkeeping department by Premier League and Three Lions icon Steven Gerrard.

Everton’s Jordan Pickford has spent the bulk of the last decade as England’s first choice but is being pushed hard by Trafford.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Playing time has been evenly split between the pair across the last two international breaks and Trafford was given the gloves against Spain on Sunday (November 15).

He delivered a stellar display in the 3-2 Nations League win, intensifying calls for him to replace Pickford as the number one.

Gerrard told The Overlap Daily: “I really like Trafford, I think he’s the future. But I also like Pickford. I don’t think we can sit here after one performance and dismiss Pickford.

“We’ve probably got two England number ones and the manager’s just got the big decision and that’s why he gets the big bucks. But the future’s Trafford. I think that’s healthy.

“I don’t like it when it’s just a foregone conclusion. He’s the England number one and it doesn’t matter how he plays because he’s the outright number one. Why can’t there be competition, why can’t there be healthy competition?”

Trafford produced a stunning double save in the dying embers, enabling England to hang on and secure a valuable victory over the reigning world champions.

Gerrard said: “It made us win the game. It’s as good or as important as a goal. The second save is world class. There was also a shot straight after it which bounced just in front of him on a greasy surface and it was just like velcro.

“It just stuck to his body. I was really impressed with that as well. It looked simple on the TV but you see so many goalkeepers spill them or want to push them away. He’s just like velcro.”
